newsitem.title: USA: SOUR CRUDE PRICES IN U.S. GULF STEADY DESPITE IRAQ.
newsitem.headline: SOUR CRUDE PRICES IN U.S. GULF STEADY DESPITE IRAQ.

text.p: Arrivals of Iraq crude into the U.S. Gulf late next month are expected to torpedo sour crude prices, but thus far differentials for West Texas Sour/Midland and Eugene Island barrels have held steady.
Traders said quotes for WTS/Midland ranged around a $1.43-40 discount to the benchmark September West Texas Inetermediate, and roughly the same levels for Eugene.
"It will hit the sour prices, as soon as people realize it's coming over here," said a cash trader in the Gulf.

Informed traders said U.S. company Bayoil had signed up refiner Ashland to purchase 525,000 barrels of Iraqi Basrah Light at WTI -$2.00 for delivery between September 28-October 10. Talk of Kirkuk sales to the Gulf were not confirmed.

The supertanker Arcadia was preparing Wednesday to berth at the Turkish port of Ceyhan to lift Iraq's first oil exports under second round oil-for-food dealings. Arcadia is to lift 2.1 million barrels of Iraqi Kirkuk for Bayoil.
Outright crude prices dipped around 10-15 cents to talk at $19.80-90 a barrel, with the September/October spread at minus 20-22 cents.

NYMEX unleaded gasoline values were originally expected to deflate on less than impressive inventory data reports, but talk of a refinery problem at Exxon's Baytown, Texas catalytic cracking unit aided a price recovery.
However, a Reuters report deflated such talk, quoting an Exxon source as saying the Baytown unit is indeed running after a leak, but may shut for a one-day repair.
Grade values also held steady for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James barrels, around 15-18 cents over the WTI. Traders could not confirm fresh deals for any of the sweet grades.
